classification.difficultyReason: Find a supplementary angle and the remaining triangle angle, apply the sine rule to establish the supplied expression, then use that result in a right triangle to obtain the pole height.

content.prompt: Talia finds that the angle of elevation of the top of a pole, $A$, from $B$ is $30^\circ$, but when she walks 30 metres towards it to point $P$, the angle of elevation is $45^\circ$.

spec.description: B, P and C are collinear in that order; A is above C. BA and PA are sightlines, AC is vertical, and C has a right-angle square. BP has a double-ended dimension arrow labelled 30 below it, and AC has a double-ended dimension arrow labelled x to its right.
spec.mathematics: Angle ABC is 30°, angle APC is 45°, BP is 30 metres and AC is x.
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens are visible; no derived angle or length is supplied.

answer.short: $AP=\dfrac{30\sin30^\circ}{\sin15^\circ}$, by the sine rule in $\triangle ABP$.
answer.worked:
Since $B$, $P$ and $C$ lie on a straight line,
$$\begin{align*}\angle BPA&=180^\circ-45^\circ\\\angle BPA&=135^\circ\\\angle BAP&=180^\circ-135^\circ-30^\circ\\\angle BAP&=15^\circ\end{align*}$$
In $\triangle ABP$, the sine rule gives
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AP}{\sin30^\circ}&=\frac{30}{\sin15^\circ}\\AP&=\frac{30\sin30^\circ}{\sin15^\circ}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence, calculate the height of the pole correct to the nearest metre.

answer.worked:
In right-angled $\triangle APC$,
$$\begin{align*}x&=AP\sin45^\circ\\x&=\frac{30\sin30^\circ\sin45^\circ}{\sin15^\circ}\\x&=15(\sqrt3+1)\text{ m}\\x&\approx40.98\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
The pole is $41\text{ m}$ high, to the nearest metre.
